findings: Brooklyn's brownstone names came first. Cobble Hill (1960), Boerum Hill (1966) and Carroll Gardens (1966) show up in Times headlines and summaries in the 1960s. Manhattan's loft-district names followed in the 1970s: SoHo in 1970, NoHo in 1975 and Tribeca in 1976.
SoHo went from nothing to everywhere. All 10 matching articles from the 1960s are about London. The count rose to 649 in the 1970s and 4,921 in the 2000s.

Most portmanteau names flopped. BoCoCa, ProCro, SoBro, SoHa and the Piano District never reached 50 articles in any decade. ProCro first appeared in April 2011, in a story about an assemblyman's bill to penalize brokers who invent neighborhood names.
SoHa kept moving. The Times put it at 104th to 107th Streets in 1996, south of Columbia in 1999 and 96th to 113th Streets in 2002.

Some old names faded, then came back. Hell's Kitchen matched 113 articles before 1950 and nine in the 1950s, then 562 in the 2000s. Ditmas Park drew one article in each of the 1950s and 1960s, then 159 in the 1990s.
Hudson Yards started from zero. No article matches before 2001. With more than three years still to go, the 2020s already equal the 2010s, at 410 articles each.
